text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Convict MARGARET CATCHPOLE, who was twice sentenced to death for stealing a horse and escaping from jail, and was transported to Botany Bay for life, was born in 1762.
Austrian composer JOHANN STRAUSS was born in 1804.

Pioneer lottery promoter GEORGE ADAMS, who ran horserace sweepstakes for the Tattersall's Club from the Marble Bar in his Hotel and eventually moved to Queensland and Tasmania to keep ahead of gambling laws, was born in 1839.
Russian novelist MAXIM GORKY was born in 1868.

German-born Swiss scientist ALBERT EINSTEIN, who received the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1921 and published the theory of relativity, was born in 1879. His work on the creation of the first atomic bomb is now part of history, and when hearing of
the annihilation of Hiroshima, he said "Had I known, I would have become a plumber".
Australian actor, theatrical producer and director JOHN McCALLUM, was born in 1918.
American composer (producer of MICHAEL JACKSON'S "Thriller") QUINCY JONES, was born in 1933.
English actor MICHAEL CAINE was born in 1933.
British singer/songwriter PETER SKELLERN was born in 1947. His hits include "You're A Lady" (1972) and "Hold On To Love"(1975)
UK singer/songwriter JONA LEWIE, who had a hit with "Stop The Cavalry"(1980), was born in 1947.
PRINCE ALBERT OF MONACO was born in 1958.
** EVENTS **
1757 : British Admiral JOHN BYNG was shot by a firing
squad for his bungled attempt to relieve the island of Minorca threatened by the French fleet, "pour encourager les autres", as Voltaire commented.
1861 : The great bell of Westminster in London repeatedly
marked the hour with 13 chimes, which was seen as a token of ill for the British Royal Family. Within 24 hours, the DUCHESS OF KENT died.
1864 : SAMUEL BAKER discovered another source of the
Nile in East Africa and named it Lake Albert Nyanza.
1891 : Eleven Italian members of a secret society, known
at the time as the Mafia, were accused of murdering a local Police Chief. When aquitted, an angry mob lynched them.
1883 : KARL MARX, German philosopher and economist, died
in London. He published, with FRIEDRICH ENGELS, the Communist Manifesto.
1900 : The botantist HUGO De VRIES rediscovered MENDEL's
laws of heredity.
1932 : GEORGE EASTMAN, the man who invented the Kodak
camera, committed suicide.
1938 : HITLER drove into Austria and made the once

independent nation just another province of Germany. He made a triumphant return to Vienna - the capital of his native land. He was greeted by enthusiastic crowds. HITLER was now the ruler of an empire of 74 million people.
1945 : The heaviest bomb of World War Two, the 22,000
pound "Grand Slam", was dropped by the RAF's Dambuster Squadron in Germany on the Bielefeld railway viaduct.
1956 : In a budget designed to combat inflation the
Australian government increased sales tax on cars, petrol, cigarettes, beer and spirits.
1964 : JACK RUBY was convicted of murdering LEE HARVEY
OSWALD, the alleged killer of United States President John F. Kennedy. 52 year-old RUBY claimed "I did it for Jackie".
1966 : Britain's first coloured police officer, MUHAMMAD
YUSUF DAAR, was sworn in.
1975 : American actress SUSAN HAYWARD died.
1976 : BUSBY BERKELEY, U.S. director and choreographer,
died. Best known for his lavish mass choreography in the films "42nd Street", "Gold Diggers of 1933" and "Roman Scandals".
1979 : Australia media mogul KERRY PACKER had talks with
the chairman of the Australian Cricket Board BOB PARISH. Two months later a deal had been done giving PACKER the rights to promote, televise and market cricket for ten years.
1989 : Former world chess champion ANATOLY KARPOV was
elected to the revamped Soviet parliament.
1991 : American playwright and director HOWARD ASHMAN
("Little Shop Of Horrors"), died.
1994 : The price of shares in the PAUL HOGAN film
"Lightning Jack" tumbled on the Australian sharemarket following critical newspaper reports about the film in the United States.
1996 : U.S. President BILL CLINTON committed US$100
million for an anti-terrorism pact with Israel to track down and root out Islamic militants.
